children: Shares of Greenland Energy surged after the company said it had extended a farm-out agreement with 80 Mile related to two exploration wells in East Greenland's Jameson Land Basin.
Shares were up 51% at $4.40 as of midday Thursday. The stock has slid 57% this year.

The company said the longstop date applicable to one of the exploration wells covered by the farm-out agreement was extended from Dec. 31, 2026 to Dec. 31, 2028. The longstop date on the second well was extended from Dec. 31, 2027 by one year.

The deed signed by Greenland Energy and 80 Mile gives the former company full responsibility to secure and maintain permits and approvals required for drilling in the Basin. 80 Mile is responsible for other government approvals required under the farm-out agreement.
Greenland Energy said it will pay 80 Mile a fee of 500,000 pounds (around $661,000) as consideration for entering into the deed.

"This amendment provides the additional time and a clear framework for us to continue advancing the Jameson Land program while the required permitting process progresses," Chief Executive Robert Price said. "Importantly, the underlying Farm-Out Agreement remains in full force and effect, and the revised timetable allows us to preserve the substantial operational preparation already undertaken while aligning future activity with the necessary regulatory approvals."
